item.title: CNN-Based Locked Mode Detection and Prospects for Prediction Utilizing Density Fluctuation Signals
item.description: arXiv:2611.28266v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The deceleration of Magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) modes in tokamak plasmas is an observed behavior commonly associated with growing mode amplitude. As rotating MHD modes decelerate to a non-rotating state, they can form Locked Modes (LMs), which can degrade plasma confinement and cause disruptions. LMs therefore pose a serious threat to the sustained operation of otherwise-stable plasmas in Fusion Pilot Plants (FPPs). Identification of MHD modes and any subsequent locking is typically performed with an array of magnetic signals; these magnetic signals may not survive in the harsh reactor environment of an FPP and external magnetic measurements are delayed by magnetic diffusion through the tokamak shielding. This work uses the Radial Interferometer Polarimeter (RIP) as an alternative diagnostic to identify the slowing of rotating MHD modes into LMs. Because this fluctuation-based approach relies on observing prior mode rotation, detection and prediction are restricted to LMs with prior rotation and exclude born-locked modes. Labels were constructed to train a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to distinguish MHD modes that lock from those that may appear to approach a locking state but ultimately do not lock. The trained CNN learned to identify low-frequency, descending MHD modes but struggled to distinguish modes that would continue toward locking from those that would not. A second-stage detection method significantly improved performance, detecting 88.5% of LMs with a precision of 83.7% by applying persistence and classification-margin filters to the CNN output. These results demonstrate the capability of an FPP-relevant, non-magnetic diagnostic for accurate LM detection while also identifying fundamental limitations in the achievable prediction time using a fluctuation-based approach.
item.dc:creator: Randall Clark, Maxim Nurgaliev, Georgy Subbotin, Jie Chen, Terry L. Rhodes, Dmitri M. Orlov

item.title: Statistical Signatures of Velocity-Space Turbulence in the Earth's Magnetosheath
item.description: arXiv:2611.28546v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In collisionless plasmas, the particle distributions are often far from local thermodynamic equilibrium, providing a significant source of free energy that leads to complex velocity-space dynamics. In turbulent plasmas, the possibility of a cascade of the free energy in velocity space, analogous to the spatial cascade of fluid and electromagnetic field energies, has been suggested. However, observational evidence of plasma turbulence throughout phase space remains limited. Using measurements from the Magnetospheric Multiscale mission in a special campaign in the Earth's magnetosheath, we present the first statistical study of signatures consistent with velocity-space turbulence across a wide range of plasma conditions. We observe two main populations in the ion velocity-space spectrum -- an isotropic $-3/2$ spectrum and an anisotropic $-2$ spectrum organized by the ion $\beta$ and bulk flow. In addition, the spectral power laws in the spatial and velocity domains are uncorrelated, while the velocity-space spectral index is correlated with estimated real-space energy transfer rates. These results reveal how the ion spectral properties are systematically organized by plasma conditions and related to real-space turbulence. This connection has broad implications for turbulence and the energy partition between thermal and non-thermal particles in space and astrophysical plasmas.
item.dc:creator: Tien Vo, Robert Ergun, Alexandros Chasapis, Oreste Pezzi, Andrea Larosa, Sergio Servidio, Luca Sorriso-Valvo, Viet Doan, Paul Cassak, Trevor Bowen, Yi Qi

item.title: Formation of Multiple BGK-like Structures in the Time-asymptotic State of Collisionless Vlasov-Poisson Plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2611.28898v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The time-asymptotic state of a finite-amplitude perturbation in a collisionless and Maxwellian plasma is typically represented as a steady state of two non-linearly superposed, counter-propagating Bernstein-Greene-Kruskal (BGK) modes. Using high-resolution Vlasov-Poisson simulations, we show that the plasma evolves self-consistently into a time-asymptotic state of multiple vortex-like structures that gradually fill the phase-space and reduce filamentation. This occurs without the need for external forcing or the presence of an energetic plasma population. This finding suggests that the time-asymptotic regime of the plasma is rather akin to a non-linear superposition of multiple BGK-like modes associated with nearly constant phase-speed waves. The electric field and the space-averaged particle distribution function exhibit a power-law broad spectrum, which is consistent with an energy cascade towards smaller scales in both position and velocity spaces.
item.dc:creator: Hugo A. Carril, Jorge A. Gidi, Roberto E. Navarro, Jaime A. Araneda

item.title: Single-Shot Single-Stage Stellarators
item.description: arXiv:2611.29090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In stellarator design, the plasma and the coils are so geometrically complex that they are usually designed separately, so that a high-performance plasma may be impossible to reproduce with coils that can actually be manufactured and assembled. We present a new method to close this gap. In this framework, the plasma shape is optimized while, for every candidate shape, near-optimal coils that satisfy hard engineering limits are found. Without any manually-tuned weights, the method steers the plasma towards shapes that real coils can produce. Moreover, we demonstrate the first single-shot optimization runs starting from tokamak ``cold-starts''. From a single-shot cold-start, we design a finite-$\beta$ stellarator comparable to reactor-scaled NCSX, as well as a compact aspect-ratio 2.5 and $\langle\beta\rangle=2\%$ quasi-axisymmetric stellarator with one field period and self-consistent bootstrap current. Starting from a boundary derived from W7-X, we design a quasi-isodynamic stellarator with reactor-relevant stability properties. We then use this to warm-start an optimization for a single coil-set solution that produces a high-performance QI stellarator at every pressure value from vacuum to $\langle\beta\rangle=4\%$, addressing directly the ``start-up'' phase of a reactor. The self-consistent free-boundary solutions for these stellarators typically have better coils than a traditional separate-design approach, at comparable or better plasma performance, illustrating that robust single-stage methods are possible and providing a direct route to the design of reactor-scale stellarators.
item.dc:creator: Pedro F. Gil, Lanke Fu, Alan A. Kaptanoglu

item.title: Electron Parameters in H2:Ar:CH4 Plasma Maintained by Microwave and Laser Radiation
item.description: arXiv:2611.29229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electron parameters in an atmospheric-pressure hybrid plasma in the 95H2:3Ar:2CH4 mixture maintained by pulsed-periodic microwave radiation (2.47 GHz) and CO2 laser radiation (10.6 {\mu}m) were studied. The plasma was generated in a quasi-cylindrical reactor, which was a resonator for TM011-mode microwave radiation. It was shown that in the hybrid plasma emission spectra the H{\alpha} and H{\betta} lines are strongly broadened and can be approximated by the sum of two Lorentzian contours (dual-Lorentzian approximation). The Stark broadening of the H{\alpha} and H{\betta} lines was used to measure the electron density in the plasma, and the ratio of their intensities allowed to estimate the electron temperature. To simplify the description of the hybrid plasma properties the concept of two plasma states caused by the pulsed injection of laser energy into the plasma was introduced. The hybrid plasma state, corresponding to the plasma state during the laser pulse, is characterized by a high electron density of (1-2.5)*10^17 cm-3 and an electron temperature of ~0.5-0.6 eV. The electron density in the state corresponding to the time intervals between laser pulses (1.8*10^14-5*10^15 cm-3) is more than an order of magnitude lower than the electron density in the first state, but it is 2-10 times higher than the electron density in microwave plasma ((1-5)*10^14 cm-3). The electron temperature in this state is 0.16-0.24 eV. The radius of the dense plasma region with an electron density of ~10^17 cm-3 is estimated to be ~0.5-1 mm.
item.dc:creator: Svetlana Avtaeva, Alexey Medvedev

item.title: A novel mechanism for coherent radio emission: particle-in-cell simulations
item.description: arXiv:2611.29352v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It has been established that electron (phase-space) holes, i.e., EHs, can arise from the nonlinear relaxation of the electron beam instability. Excitation of electromagnetic waves related to the EHs is, however, still not fully understood. Using 2.5-dimensional particle-in-cell simulations, we systematically investigate the nonlinear evolution of the (moderately relativistic) electron bi-stream instability (a special case of the electron beam instability where the densities of the two counter-propagating energetic electron beams are equivalent) in charge- and current-neutralized plasmas under weak and strong magnetizations. This study provides new insights into the wave excitation, the nonlinear wave-particle interactions, the formation of non-Maxwellian features, and the anisotropic electron heating in magnetized plasmas, with potential implications for coherent radio emission in astrophysical plasmas (e.g., solar zebra-pattern bursts).
item.dc:creator: Xiaowei Zhou, Dejin Wu, Ling Chen, Zongjun Ning

item.title: Radial Evolution of Correlation Anisotropy in PUNCH Observations of the Young Solar Wind
item.description: arXiv:2611.29573v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Solar wind turbulence, evolving in the presence of a mean magnetic field, large-scale shear, and expansion, exhibits several types of anisotropy, including wavevector anisotropy and variance anisotropy. As the solar wind expands from the corona into the interplanetary space, the magnetically controlled outer corona transitions into the dynamic and less constrained solar wind, and fluctuations may evolve toward isotropy. This is suggestive of an evolution of anisotropy with distance from the Sun, a feature observed in earlier results using surveys of in-situ data, as well as more limited images of solar wind density from STEREO. Here we confirm and expand on those results employing data from the PUNCH mission, whose wide-field, high-cadence imaging enables anisotropy tracking at different heliospheric positions. We evaluate a two-dimensional (2D) correlation function $C(\ell_{\perp}, \ell_{\parallel})$ of polarized white-light brightness as a function of radial $\ell_\parallel$ and transverse $\ell_\perp$ scales to infer the nature of density anisotropy and its development in space. At larger heliocentric distances ($\sim 100 R_\odot$), circular contours of the correlation function indicate a transition toward approximate isotropy. The correlation structure at heliocentric distances from $30R_\odot$ to $60R_\odot$ preferentially extends along the radial direction, which might imply the possible dominance of the two-dimensional variation in the transverse plane. In this way, the very large field of view of PUNCH images reveal a fundamental transition of solar wind turbulence toward isotropy.

item.title: Relativistic Harmonic Generation in Spatiotemporal Plasma Photonic Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.30084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatiotemporal photonic crystals offer a route to controlling the frequency, momentum, and energy of light. Extending this capability to relativistic laser intensities calls for a plasma-based platform. Here we propose a spatiotemporal plasma photonic crystal (SPPC) formed at a solid surface driven by intense pump pulses, with a separate probe interacting with the resulting modulation. The spatial and temporal periodicity of the SPPC determines the allowed harmonic frequencies and emission angles, while its complex Floquet bands explain how the probe draws energy from the modulation. Beyond harmonic generation, this picture predicts wavelength-dependent probe amplification as the probe accesses amplifying modes of the SPPC, providing an experimentally testable connection between the band structure and energy transfer. Agreement with particle-in-cell simulations supports this interpretation.
item.dc:creator: Haojie Zhang, Boyuan Li, Xiangyan An, Rong Huang, Feng Liu, Zheng-Ming Sheng, Min Chen

item.title: Plasma-enabled magnet-free LSW search for eV-scale axions with laser-stimulated regeneration
item.description: arXiv:2611.30098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In conventional light-shining-through-a-wall (LSW) experiments, strong magnetic fields mediate the conversion of photons into axions and their subsequent reconversion into photons. At eV-scale axion masses, however, photon--axion phase mismatch causes these conversions to lose coherence, substantially reducing the experimental sensitivity. We propose a magnet-free LSW scheme that addresses this limitation via plasma-based axion generation and laser-stimulated regeneration. At low laser intensity, a two-color dispersion-matched source generates axions in a narrow mass range set by the plasma dispersion. At relativistic laser intensity, a single-pulse plasma-broadened source generates axions over a broad mass range, as shown by particle-in-cell simulations. The Fourier spectrum of the source term $\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ broadens around the laser branch, consistent with mixing between the laser and low-frequency plasma waves. For axion detection behind the wall, a counter-propagating laser stimulates axion decay into a detectable signal photon and a second photon emitted into the laser mode, with the laser frequency chosen to satisfy phase matching. For representative parameters, the requirement of at least one regenerated photon yields projected upper limits on the axion-photon coupling on the order $10^{-7}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ over $m_a=0.1$--$1\,\mathrm{eV}$.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyan An, Min Chen, Yipeng Wu, Boyuan Li, Wenchao Yan, Peng Yuan, Binbin Yan, Feng Liu, Zhengming Sheng, Jie Zhang

item.title: High-rate accumulation of ${8.9\times10^9}$ positrons using a linac-driven buffer-gas trap combined with a SiC remoderator
item.description: arXiv:2611.30238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report the accumulation of $(8.9 \pm 0.9)\times10^9$ positrons in less than 35 minutes in a Penning--Malmberg trap connected to the GBAR electron-linac-based positron source. To our knowledge, this exceeds the largest previously reported trapped-positron population by more than a factor of two and was achieved at an 18-fold higher average accumulation rate of $4.5\times10^6$~e$^+$/s. The accumulated positron clouds are intended for the creation of dense positronium targets to produce keV-antihydrogen beams by charge exchange with antiprotons delivered by the CERN AD/ELENA facility. The system combines a low-energy electron linac, a modified Surko-type buffer-gas trap enhanced by a silicon carbide remoderator, and a high-field Penning--Malmberg trap operated as a positron accumulator. Time-resolved annihilation measurements provide insight into the capture and cooling dynamics, while comparisons of CO$_2$ and SF$_6$ show that the trapping signal reaches saturation at lower gas pressures with SF$_6$. Measurements show that the SiC-remoderator-based trapping scheme more than doubles the trapping efficiency, contributing to a more than threefold increase in the positron accumulation rate compared with the original configuration.

item.title: Bypassing the Nanoampere Limit: A Thick-Target Methodology for Ultra-Low-Energy Resonances in the $^{11}$B(p,$\alpha$)2$\alpha$ Reaction
item.description: arXiv:2611.30439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Precise measurements of the low-energy cross section for the $^{11}$B(p,$\alpha$)2$\alpha$ reaction is critical for nuclear astrophysics and fusion energy research, yet such measurements are experimentally demanding due to the reaction's extremely small cross section. Conventional thin-target experiments are fundamentally limited to nanoampere beam currents, which restrict count rates to impractical levels at ultra-low proton energies. To overcome this limitation, we report a correction-free thick-target methodology capable of operating at beam currents of 20-60 microamperes, corresponding to a gain of over three orders of magnitude. Monte Carlo simulations of the full reaction kinematics are employed to determine the absolute reaction yield, eliminating the requirement for empirical normalization factors. At the well-known 148~keV (c.m.) resonance peak, our extracted resonance energy ($E_{\mathrm{r}} = 148.0$~keV) and level width ($\Gamma_{\mathrm{cm}} = 5.3$~keV) are demonstrated in good agreement with published data. A scheme via comparing the measured reaction probability with a theoretical extrapolation result is furtherly presented to probe low-energy resonances below 100~keV region. Preliminary measurements at proton energies of 75~keV and 100~keV reveal no evidence for additional low-energy resonances. This work provides a robust new methodology to measure cross section and resonance parameters for the p$^{11}$B reaction and offers a highly efficient tool for systematic resonance searches in the ultra-low-energy regime.
item.dc:creator: Xu-Yang Luo, Wen-Qing Wei, Shi-zheng Zhang, Wen Jiang, Bu-bo Ma, Zi-qian Zhao, Zhao Wang, Guo-Dong Wang, Lu-Lin Shi, Rui Cheng, Yan-Shi Zhang, Di Luo, Xiao Xiao, Guan-Chao Zhao, Bing Liu, Dieter H. H. Hoffmann, Jie-Ru Ren, Yong-Tao Zhao

item.title: A particle method for the space homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30808v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a structure preserving particle method to numerically approximate the spatially homogeneous Lenard-Balescu equation for collisional plasmas. The Lenard-Balescu operator is an improvement of the Landau equation with a dielectric function taking the dynamic screening effect into account. Our particle method is based on the variational formulation of the Lenard-Balescu equation under suitable regularization analogous to the strategy followed for the Landau collision operator in [12]. The method guarantees the conservation laws and the entropy dissipation at the semi-discrete level. The novel difficulty of the nonlocal nonlinear dependence of the dielectric function is tackled by rewriting it as integrals in terms of orthogonal and parallel components to the frequency variable. This equivalent form reduces the evaluation of the dielectric function to numerically computing an integral of the directional derivative of the solution on a hyperplane orthogonal to the frequency variable and its one-dimensional Hilbert transform. An efficient implementation of the numerical approximation for the Lenard-Balescu kernel is derived by exploiting this expression of the dielectric function. We finally validate our method by means of several numerical tests, further allowing us to explore qualitative properties of the Lenard-Balescu equation.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Antonio Carrillo, Timon Gutleb, Andrea Medaglia, Yijia Tang

item.title: Exact 1D Nonlinear Solutions for Proton-Driven Plasma Wakefields
item.description: arXiv:2607.06458v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The analytical modeling of a plasma wakefield driven by a relativistic proton beam is an element in optimizing advanced plasma-based acceleration schemes. In this work, we present a 1D nonlinear fluid framework under the quasi-static approximation to describe the wake potential excited by a positively charged proton driver which attracts background electrons into a density compression rather than expelling them. We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using a two-bunch scheme, our piecewise-event integration model is validated to high numerical accuracy ($\sim 10^{-11}~\mathrm{GV/m}$) against independent phase-space quadrature of cold-fluid solutions, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ ramped micro-bunch train with fixed $2\pi$ spacing, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a piecewise analytical scaling model. This formulation maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic post-train residual wake plateau, which is determined exactly by the conserved vacuum Hamiltonian invariant evaluated at the final bunch-train exit state. Furthermore, the framework estimates the onset of nonlinear phase-slippage that arrests growth and causes the transient wakefield overshoot to decay toward the residual horizon. Providing immediate 1D analytical benchmarks, this computationally inexpensive tool offers a reproducible baseline for verifying 1D fluid and multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) codes. It also provides a tractable starting point for exploring asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles relevant to transformer-ratio optimization.
item.dc:creator: D. Tsiklauri

item.title: Comparative qualification of advanced plasma-facing materials for fusion pilot plants through public- and private-sector experiments in DIII-D
item.description: arXiv:2607.23400v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A coordinated DIII-D campaign involving four private fusion developers and 12 participating institutions comparatively assessed 44 advanced plasma-facing materials, including the first DIII-D divertor exposure of neutron-irradiated W, to support fusion pilot plant wall and divertor material qualification. Samples were exposed using the Divertor Materials Evaluation System (DiMES) under Ohmic, L-mode, and H-mode conditions with edge-localized modes, at 0.2-2.5 MW m$^{-2}$ on flush geometries and 10-15 MW m$^{-2}$ on 10$^\circ$ angled geometries. Engineered tungsten architectures retained integrity; long-fiber Wf/W showed the clearest crack-arrest behavior. W-Re and K-doped W showed near-ITER-W-like responses, while additively manufactured W-Ta showed heat-flux-sensitive mass losses of 0.64 mg for the flat sample and 2.19-2.87 mg for angled samples. After irradiation to 0.3 dpa at 550$^\circ$C, neutron-irradiated ITER-grade W retained 2.8 times more deuterium than pristine W, while TiB$2$ showed the lowest D$2$ release in the Ohmic set. VTaHfMo was the most stable refractory multi-principal-element alloy. NbC and (Nb${0.5}$Ta${0.5}$)C retained integrity with 0.02-0.03 mg mass loss, whereas ZrC lost 7 mg. CVD SiC retained macroscopic integrity but exhibited an effective Si erosion yield of 0.5, about 5-10 times above prior DIII-D trends. Renewable boron pebble rods underwent plasma-driven recession; 13% of released boron was ionized near the outer strike point and up to 50% was recovered locally. Initial in-situ Cr gross-erosion measurements yielded effective erosion yields of order $10^{-2}$. Together, these results provide cross-material benchmarks for fusion pilot plant down-selection and future AI/ML-assisted plasma-facing-material development.

item.title: Direct, Collision-Operator-Free Simulation of Electron-Ion Transport in Magnetized and Unmagnetized Plasmas
item.description: arXiv:2608.24012v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Accurate electron-ion collision models are central to predicting transport in fusion and space plasmas, yet collision operators and Monte Carlo collision models assume that a charged particle meets one partner at a time and that its successive encounters are independent. However, an electron that turns back along the magnetic field passes the same ions again. We solve the Newton-Lorentz equations for test electrons among static ions with a prescribed Debye-screened potential. The method combines force summation within an interaction radius, a time-symmetric particle pusher, and adaptive time stepping, enabling stable and scalable simulations in unmagnetized and magnetized plasmas. Using simulation-based measures of momentum relaxation and cross-field diffusion, we compare the simulations with a reference in the same model that treats every encounter as independent. Without a magnetic field the scattering rate reproduces the binary-collision rate for the same potential to within 2%. When the gyroradius is smaller than the Debye length, the scattering rate stays within 10% of the reference, but the cross-field diffusion coefficient exceeds it by a factor that grows with the field, up to 17. The excess comes from repeated passes of the same ions, whose guiding-center displacements add up: when the ions are replaced by new random ones many times per scattering time, so that a returning electron meets different ions, most of the excess disappears. The framework therefore provides a computational benchmark for testing and improving reduced collision operators and transport models.
item.dc:creator: Keheng Zhu, Jian Liu, Chaozhou Mou, Senran Lin, Wei Zhang

item.title: Thresholdless IBW Emission and Alpha-to-Thermal-Ion Energy Channeling via Pole Resonance of Fusion-Product Ions
item.description: arXiv:2609.07732v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fusion reactions can release a substantial fraction, and in aneutronic reactions nearly all, of their energy as the kinetic energy of fusion-product ions. In magnetized plasmas, these energetic ions can form ring distributions in velocity space. Such distributions can drive Dory-Guest-Harris (DGH) electrostatic instabilities, but these self-instabilities require a finite energetic-ion density and can be stabilized by a thermal background. We show that the same background can instead enable a distinct instability mechanism: a cyclotron pole of the minority energetic-ion susceptibility destabilizes a stable ion Bernstein wave (IBW) eigenmode. When the energetic-ion harmonic is distinct from the thermal-ion harmonics, exact root-pole resonance is thresholdless in the ideal collisionless limit. A species-resolved power balance shows that the energetic ions supply the free energy while the thermal plasma receives it. In the LAPD proton--alpha example, $99.96\%$ of the alpha-particle power loss enters the coherent proton response. This self-excited, ion-directed transfer provides a possible linear building block for alpha-particle energy channeling in proton-Boron11 fusion.
item.dc:creator: Hong Qin, Nathaniel J. Fisch

item.title: A Semi-Lagrangian Adaptive Rank (SLAR) Method for High-Dimensional Vlasov Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2510.24861v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend our previous work on a semi-Lagrangian adaptive rank (SLAR) integrator, in the finite difference framework for nonlinear Vlasov-Poisson systems, to the general high-order tensor setting. The proposed scheme retains the high-order accuracy of semi-Lagrangian methods, ensuring stability for large time steps and avoiding dimensional splitting errors. The primary contribution of this paper is the novel extension of the algorithm from the matrix to the high-dimensional tensor setting, which enables the simulation of Vlasov models in up to six dimensions. The key technical components include (1) a third-order high-dimensional polynomial reconstruction that scales as $O(d^2)$, providing a point-wise approximation of the solution at the foot of characteristics in a semi-Lagrangian scheme; (2) a recursive hierarchical adaptive cross approximation of high-order tensors in a hierarchical Tucker format, characterized by a tensor tree; (3) a low-complexity Poisson solver in the hierarchical Tucker format that leverages the FFT for efficiency. The computed adaptive rank kinetic solutions exhibit low-rank structures within branches of the tensor tree resulting in substantial computational savings in both storage and time. The resulting algorithm achieves a computational complexity of $O(d^4 N r^{3+\lceil\log_2d\rceil})$, where $N$ is the number of grid points per dimension, $d$ is the problem dimension, and $r$ is the maximum rank in the tensor tree, overcoming the curse of dimensionality. Through extensive numerical tests, we demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed algorithm and highlight its ability to capture complex solution structures while maintaining a computational complexity that scales linearly with $N$.
item.dc:creator: Nanyi Zheng, William A. Sands, Daniel Hayes, Andrew J. Christlieb, Jing-Mei Qiu

item.title: Peristaltic Flow in Compressible, Ideal Magnetohydrodynamics: A Mechanism For Solar Spicules
item.description: arXiv:2606.09626v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an analytical model for peristaltic transport within compressible, ideal magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). By employing a small-amplitude perturbation expansion, under a thin-tube long-wavelength approximation with a uniform axial background magnetic field, we study non-linear coupling between thermodynamic pressure variations and Maxwell's magnetic tension stresses. The resulting net time-averaged conserved mass flux $\langle \dot{M} \rangle$ is calculated. When applied to solar chromospheric spicules under equipartition constraints ($\beta \sim 1$), where sound speed matches the Alfv{\'e}n speed, we find $\langle \dot{M} \rangle = 8\epsilon^2/(M^2-1)^2$. Because the denominator remains strictly positive across all operational supersonic Mach numbers ($M \approx 2\text{--}10$), upward-propagating mechanical disturbances drive a highly directional, collimated upward flow which we interpret as a spicule. Estimates show that for observationally realistic magnetosonic waves with amplitudes of $\approx 10\%$, the peristaltic mechanism generates a localized mass flux up to $\approx 100$ times that of the solar wind. We show that because high-Mach waves suffer strong compressible choking, small-amplitude perturbations preferentially select low-supersonic modes ($M \approx 1.05\text{--}2.0$) to drive spicule-level mass loading. We propose an explicit observational signature of this mechanism, wherein the launch of individual spicular jets is directly preceded by magnetosonic wave trains detectable as localized intensity modulations. Beyond solar chromospheric application, the model may be applicable to traveling magnetic field pinches in laboratory plasma devices and astrophysical mass-loading processes in stellar winds and inner regions of magnetized accretion disks.
item.dc:creator: D. Tsiklauri
